title: [review] local-fact: verifier clock spoof re-admits revoked fact (expiry killed only by GPS time)
description: Codereview pass 2 (security, kimi-k3) on project-LICHEN-worker6-xeli surfaced a residual rooted in the local-fact 'Freshness and Revocation' text (spec/06-security.md 8.13.1, lines ~1153-1173, from unmerged b4fu ca2f9161d9) — NOT in xeli's restart-continuity paragraph, so filed separately. The revocation-by-non-renewal path leaves the revoked fact as the highest-seq fact, so only its lichen:expiry kills it. A radio adversary (in LICHEN's threat model) that spoofs a verifier's GPS/RTC clock BACKWARD makes an expired revoked fact look unexpired; the seq check passes (it is the highest seen), so the revoked grant is re-admitted until the clock recovers or the fact truly expires. Fix direction: (a) make expiry checks robust to clock rollback (e.g. verifier clamps expiry comparison against a monotonic elapsed-time floor or the highest observed wall-clock, similar to xeli's issuer-side max(floor+1, time-derived) clamp), or (b) require issuers to actively supersede (issue a higher-seq replacement with short expiry) rather than rely on non-renewal alone. Adjacent to xeli (issuer-side GPS spoof, fixed there) and b4fu. Decide with the 8.13.1 freshness model.
